rationale: Across published cohorts detailing individuals with NAV3-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621182), the core phenotypic manifestations comprise static global developmental delay/intellectual disability, poor or absent speech, microcephaly, behavioral abnormalities, dysmorphic facial features, and variable skeletal or ocular anomalies. Seizures have been noted in occasional individuals, but early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, progressive neurodegeneration, developmental regression, and major structural brain malformations such as lissencephaly or holoprosencephaly have not been documented in NAV3 patients. Such findings are characteristic of distinct neurodevelopmental entities (e.g., SCN3A- or ASTN1-associated disorders), thereby serving as exclusionary discriminators against primary NAV3-related disorder.

evidence.text: Reported 11 individuals from seven families with NAV3 pathogenic variants exhibiting intellectual disability, microcephaly, skeletal deformities, ocular anomalies, and behavioral abnormalities without progressive neurodegeneration, severe visceral malformations, or lissencephaly/holoprosencephaly.

source.title: Variants of NAV3, a neuronal morphogenesis protein, cause intellectual disability, developmental delay, and microcephaly
source.quote: We report eleven individuals from seven families harboring predicted pathogenic biallelic, de novo, and heterozygous variants in the NAV3 gene... All affected individuals have intellectual disability (ID), microcephaly, skeletal deformities, ocular anomalies, and behavioral issues.

evidence.text: Five patients from three consanguineous families with biallelic truncating NAV3 variants manifested dysmorphism, intellectual disability, developmental delay, absent speech, and behavioral abnormalities without progressive degeneration or cleft lip/palate.

source.title: Further evidence of biallelic NAV3 variants associated with recessive neurodevelopmental disorder with dysmorphism, developmental delay, intellectual disability …
source.quote: They had normal height, absent speech, no cleft lip or cleft … with biallelic variants in NAV3 with variable dysmorphic features … Here, we report five patients from three unrelated consanguineous families segregating autosomal recessive NDD. Patients have symptoms of dysmorphism, intellectual disability, developmental delay, and behavioral abnormalities.

evidence.text: Recessive NAV3 disruption was documented in a patient presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, speech delay, and seizures as part of a complex neurodevelopmental disorder.

source.title: Mutated neuron navigator 3 as a candidate gene for a rare neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: We describe a Saudi proband presenting a complex recessive neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD)... hallmark phenotypes such as ID, GDD, seizures, speech delay

evidence.text: In contrast to NAV3-related disorder, disorders with severe cortical malformations such as lissencephaly or polymicrogyria are characteristic of other neuronal migration defects (e.g. ASTN1-associated disorders).

source.title: Bi-allelic variants in neuronal adhesion molecule astrotactin 1 gene ASTN1 cause diverse neurodevelopmental disorders
source.quote: Additionally, we add to the neuroradiographic phenotype of this condition, which can be normal, mildly dysmorphic (a thin corpus callosum and cerebellar dysgenesis), or severely dysmorphic (polymicrogyria and lissencephaly).

evidence.text: Severe early-infantile epileptic encephalopathy and cortical malformations occur at high penetrance in SCN3A-associated channelopathies, distinguishing them from NAV3 disorders where such severe epileptic encephalopathies are not characteristic.

source.title: SCN3A‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: A Spectrum of Epilepsy and Brain Malformation
source.quote: Of 22 patients with pathogenic SCN3A variants, most had treatment-resistant epilepsy beginning in the first year of life (16/21, 76%; median onset, 2 weeks), with severe or profound developmental delay (15/20, 75%). Many, but not all (15/19, 79%), exhibited malformations of cortical development.

new_directions.question_text: Does neuroimaging across all documented biallelic and monoallelic NAV3 patients reveal any subclinical corpus callosum or white matter anomalies on high-resolution brain MRI?
new_directions.rationale: NAV3 is involved in microtubule stabilization, neurite outgrowth, and axonal guidance; systematic quantification of subtle structural brain findings (e.g., thin corpus callosum or delayed myelination) versus severe malformations is needed.

new_directions.question_text: Do monoallelic (de novo or dominant) versus biallelic loss-of-function variants in NAV3 present distinct phenotypic severity thresholds or microcephaly penetrance?
new_directions.rationale: Early publications identified both biallelic and monoallelic cases in cohorts, warranting a formal genotype-phenotype meta-analysis across all known families.
